images.caption: Figure 1:One step of a household task: picking up a cube from the counter. (a) Existing agents control the motion through a text prompt or a skill and receive no feedback or only rendered frames; after the hand misses the cube, the agent can only reword the prompt, and the hand misses again. (b) Inhabitant measures how far the hand stopped from the cube (quantitative feedback), fixes where the right hand must be at a given frame (spatial control), and grasps the cube on the next try. The frames in (a) come from our agent restricted to text prompts.

Figure 2:Overview of Inhabitant. Left: the agentπ\picontrols a pretrained motion generator𝒢\mathcal{G}by writing a control specificationcc(spatial control) and interaction eventsee. The scene simulatorℰ\mathcal{E}executes the motion, and the agent queries measurementsM⁡(q,τ)M(q,\tau)of the candidate segmentτ\tau(quantitative feedback) before it tries again, commits or rolls back (Sec.3.2). Right: one episode with Claude Opus 5.5, 13 committed segments out of 37 tries. Solid bodies: ends of committed segments, numbered in order; hollow bodies: discarded candidates; insets: three of the interactions; check mark: the success rule is satisfied.

Figure 3:Overview ofInhabit.
(a) Half-physics simulation: the hollow body shows the generated motion before execution, and the solid body shows the executed motion after scene interaction.
(b) The five goal types, illustrated on segments from an Inhabitant episode.
(c) Example tasks from each tier in the apartment, showing the body path, each object’s start position and its target.
(d) Success rule for the high-tier task in (c), with one condition per goal.
(e) The full set of 75 tasks: each circle represents one task, with one sector per goal colored as in (b), alongside three of the 31 furniture layouts.

Figure 4:Inhabitant and the three baselines on one task with the same language model; chips show which of our two interfaces each agent has and what it has in place of a missing one. Red dots: where the throws of InteractAgent†land; yellow circle: the 10 cm radius of the grasp rule; inset: a missed grasp of GEMS†. More examples are in the video on the project page.
